lessons.title: Listen and speak: a counting rhyme
lessons.objective: Listen to, say and act a short rhyme, and retell a little story with gestures.
lessons.course:
A rhyme is a short poem with words that sound the same at the end: ball – wall, hop – stop.
We say it with rhythm and gestures, and we listen to our friends.

support.title: Say the Klassia rhyme
support.text:
One, two, kick the ball,
Three, four, by the wall,
Five, six, hop, hop, hop,
Seven, eight, now we stop!

lessons.model: The adult says the rhyme with gestures: kick, point to the wall, hop, then stop with arms open.
lessons.guided: Say the rhyme line by line after the adult, then all together with the gestures. Find the words that sound the same.
lessons.exercise: Which word sounds like “ball” in the rhyme?
lessons.remediation: Say the first two lines only, with the gestures.
lessons.transfer: Teach the rhyme to a brother, a sister or a friend.

practice.prompt: Listen to the rhyme and say it after the voice.
practice.listen: One, two, kick the ball. Three, four, by the wall. Five, six, hop, hop, hop. Seven, eight, now we stop!
practice.explanation: Say each line with its gesture.

practice.prompt: Match the words that sound the same.
practice.explanation: Rhyming words end with the same sound.

practice.prompt: Put the lines of the rhyme in order.
practice.explanation: The numbers help you find the order.

lessons.title: Read: longer words in parts
lessons.objective: Read words of two and three syllables by cutting them into parts.
lessons.course:
Long words have parts called syllables. We clap for each part: foot-ball (2), skip-ping (2), bi-cy-cle (3).
We read each part, then the whole word.
lessons.model: The adult claps and reads: “hop… scotch: hopscotch. We play hopscotch in the school yard.”
lessons.guided: Clap the parts of each word, then read it. Sort the words: two claps or three claps.
lessons.remediation: Clap two-part words only (football, skipping) before three-part words.
lessons.transfer: Clap the parts of the names of your friends.

practice.prompt: Put the parts in order to read the word.
How many parts in “football”?
Which word has three parts?

lessons.title: Write: short sentences (who does what)
lessons.objective: Write a short sentence with a subject, a verb and an object, starting with a capital letter and ending with a full stop.
lessons.course:
A short sentence says who does what: Tabi kicks the ball. Bih skips the rope.
It starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

support.title: Copy with the adult
support.text:
Tabi kicks the ball.
Bih skips the rope.

lessons.model: The adult writes: “Neba throws the ball.” and points: “Who? Neba. Does what? throws. What? the ball.”
lessons.guided: Choose a name, an action and a thing from three boxes of cards. Build the sentence, read it, then write it.
lessons.exercise: Write a sentence: Ashu / plays / football.
lessons.remediation: Copy a model sentence first, then change only the name.
lessons.transfer: Write one sentence about the game you like.
lessons.materials: Cards with names, actions and things; pencil.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
practice.explanation: Who? Bih. Does what? skips. What? the rope.

practice.prompt: Write the sentence: Tabi kicks the ball.
practice.explanation: Capital letter at the start, full stop at the end.

practice.prompt: What do we put at the end of a sentence?
practice.explanation: A sentence ends with a full stop.

lessons.title: Yesterday and today: here, there, now
lessons.objective: Say what happened yesterday with regular verbs in the simple past, and use adverbs of time and place.
lessons.course:
Today we play. Yesterday we played. For many verbs, we add ed to talk about the past: jump → jumped, kick → kicked.
Adverbs of time: now, today, yesterday. Adverbs of place: here, there.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
Today I jump. Yesterday I jumped.
Come here! The ball is there.

lessons.model: The adult says: “Now I kick the ball. Yesterday I kicked the ball too.” Then points: “The ball is there. Bring it here.”
lessons.guided: Say what you do today, then what you did yesterday, adding ed. Play “here and there” with a ball.
lessons.remediation: Practise with three verbs only: play, jump, kick.
lessons.transfer: Tell an adult what you played yesterday.

practice.prompt: Add ed to talk about yesterday.
practice.text: Yesterday we jump[[ed]] and kick[[ed]] the ball.

practice.prompt: Which word tells about the past?
practice.explanation: Yesterday is the day before today.

practice.prompt: Complete: Come ___! (to the place where I am)
practice.explanation: Here is where I am; there is another place.

lessons.title: The table of 3
lessons.objective: Build the multiplication table of 3 and use it in games.
lessons.model: In a game, each team has 3 players. The adult counts: “1 team: 3 players. 2 teams: 6 players. 4 teams: 12 players.”
lessons.guided: Make groups of 3 stones. Say the table as you add a group each time.
lessons.remediation: Count in 3s with groups of objects: 3, 6, 9.
lessons.transfer: Count the legs of 3-legged stools in 3s.

practice.prompt: Complete the count in 3s.
4 teams of 3 players. How many players?

lessons.title: Tallies in 3s and telling the results
lessons.objective: Tally in 3s, collect the results of a game and present them orally.
lessons.course:
We can count tallies in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12.
After a game, we collect the results in a table and say them: “Team A scored 9, team B scored 6. Team A won.”
lessons.model: The adult tallies points in a game of marbles in groups of 3 and announces the results aloud.
lessons.guided: Play a short game. Make a tally for each point. Count in 3s and say the results to the group.
lessons.remediation: Group the tally marks in 3s with a circle before counting.
lessons.transfer: Keep the score of a game with your friends using tallies.

practice.prompt: Team A has 3 groups of 3 points. How many points?
Team A: 9 points. Team B: 6 points. Which team won?
Say the results of the game in one sentence.
practice.answer: Team A scored 9 points and won.

lessons.title: Making shapes
lessons.objective: Construct triangles, squares, rectangles and circles with sticks, string and paper.
lessons.course: We can make shapes: a triangle with 3 sticks, a square with 4 equal sticks, a rectangle with 2 long and 2 short sticks. A circle is made with a string around a can.
lessons.model: The adult places 4 equal sticks: “4 equal sides: a square.” Then 2 long and 2 short: “a rectangle.”
lessons.guided: Use sticks of the same and different lengths to make each shape. Name each shape.
lessons.exercise: How many sticks do you need for a triangle?
lessons.remediation: Copy a shape drawn on paper by putting sticks on top of it.
lessons.transfer: Draw the shape of a hopscotch game on the ground.
lessons.materials: Sticks or straws, string, a tin.

practice.prompt: How many sides does a square have?
Match each shape with how we make it.
practice.answer: triangle: 3; square: 4 equal; rectangle: 2 long, 2 short.

practice.prompt: Draw a rectangle.
practice.answer: A shape with 2 long sides and 2 short sides.
practice.explanation: Opposite sides are the same length.

lessons.title: Problems about games
lessons.objective: Choose to add, take away or share to solve a simple problem.
lessons.course:
To solve a problem, read it, find what we know and what we look for, then choose: add (more), take away (less), share (equal parts).
Neba has 12 marbles. He wins 5. More marbles: we add. 12 + 5 = 17.
lessons.model: The adult reads a problem and thinks aloud: “She loses some: that is less. I take away.”
lessons.guided: Act out each problem with marbles, then write the operation.
lessons.exercise: Bih has 18 marbles. She loses 6. How many does she have now?
lessons.remediation: Act out the problem with objects before writing the numbers.
lessons.transfer: Make up a problem about a game you play.

practice.prompt: Tabi has 10 marbles. He wins 7 more. How many marbles now?
12 marbles shared equally between 2 friends. How many each?
Ekane had 9 balls and gave away 4. What do we do?
practice.explanation: He has less: we take away. 9 − 4 = 5.

lessons.title: The five senses game
lessons.objective: Relate each sense to its organ and use the senses to recognise things.
lessons.course:
We have five senses. We see with our eyes. We hear with our ears. We smell with our nose. We taste with our tongue. We touch with our skin.
We protect our sense organs: we do not put objects in our ears or our nose, and we do not look at the sun.
lessons.model: With closed eyes, Tabi smells an orange and says: “It is an orange!” He used his nose.
lessons.guided: Play the senses game: with eyes closed, touch, smell or taste (with an adult) a safe thing and guess what it is. Say which sense you used.
lessons.exercise: Which organ do we use to hear?
lessons.remediation: Point to each organ and say its sense with the adult.
lessons.transfer: Close your eyes at home and name three sounds you hear.
lessons.materials: Safe objects to touch, smell and taste (fruits, cloth, a bell).

practice.prompt: Match each sense with its organ.
practice.answer: seeing: eyes; smelling: nose; tasting: tongue.

practice.prompt: How many senses do we have?
practice.explanation: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

practice.prompt: Which is a good way to protect our eyes?
choices: not rub them with dirty hands
practice.answer: not rub them with dirty hands
practice.explanation: Dirty hands can make our eyes sick.

lessons.title: Sur, sous, devant, derrière
lessons.objective: Dire une comptine en français et situer un objet avec sur, sous, devant et derrière.
lessons.course: Pour dire où est un objet : « Le ballon est sur la table. » (on) « Le chat est sous la chaise. » (under) « Bih est devant Neba. » (in front of) « Neba est derrière Bih. » (behind)

support.title: Comptine Klassia
support.text:
Le ballon saute, saute, saute,
sur la table, sous la chaise,
devant moi, derrière toi,
et hop, il revient à moi !

lessons.model: L’adulte pose un ballon sur la table : « Le ballon est sur la table. » Puis sous la chaise : « Le ballon est sous la chaise. »
lessons.guided: Dis la comptine avec des gestes. Puis l’adulte cache un objet ; l’enfant le trouve et dit où il était.
lessons.exercise: Le chat est en dessous de la chaise. Où est le chat ?
lessons.answer: Le chat est sous la chaise.
accept: Le chat est sous la chaise
lessons.remediation: Travaille d’abord sur et sous avec une boîte et un jouet.
lessons.transfer: Dis la comptine à quelqu’un de ta maison.
lessons.materials: Un ballon, une chaise, une boîte.

practice.prompt: Complète avec sur ou sous.
practice.text: Le livre est [[sur]] la table. Le chien est [[sous]] la table.

practice.prompt: Neba est derrière Bih. Qui est devant ?
practice.explanation: Si Neba est derrière Bih, Bih est devant Neba.

practice.prompt: Écoute et répète la comptine.
practice.listen: Le ballon saute, saute, saute, sur la table, sous la chaise, devant moi, derrière toi, et hop, il revient à moi !
practice.answer: La comptine dite avec les gestes.
practice.explanation: Fais les gestes en même temps.

lessons.title: Fair play: respect and tolerance in games
lessons.objective: Show respect and tolerance when playing with others.
lessons.course:
When we play, we respect the rules, we wait for our turn and we accept to lose. We play with every child, even if he is different from us. This is tolerance.
When we win, we do not laugh at the others. When we lose, we say “Well done” to the winner.
lessons.model: Ekane’s team loses the football match. He shakes hands with the winners and says: “Well done!”
lessons.guided: Play a short game. Before, say the rules together. After, say “Well done” to the winner.
lessons.exercise: Your team loses a game. What do you say to the winners?
lessons.remediation: Practise waiting for your turn with a ball game in a circle.
lessons.transfer: Invite a child who plays alone to join your game.
lessons.materials: A ball or a game everyone knows.

practice.prompt: Which one shows respect in a game?
A new child wants to play with you. What do you do?
practice.answer: I invite him or her to play.
accept: I invite him or her to play

practice.prompt: Match the action with the value.
pairs: saying well done to the winner

lessons.title: Weaving a paper mat
lessons.objective: Weave strips of paper over and under to make a small mat.
lessons.course:
Weaving means passing strips over and under other strips. People weave mats, baskets and caps with raffia or palm leaves.
With paper strips, we can weave a small mat: over, under, over, under.
lessons.model: The adult cuts strips in a sheet and passes a strip of another colour: “Over, under, over, under.”
lessons.guided: Weave four strips of paper into a sheet cut in strips. Change the colour each time.
lessons.exercise: What words help us to weave?
lessons.remediation: Use wide strips and only three of them.
lessons.transfer: Look at a mat or a basket at home and find the over-under pattern.
lessons.materials: Coloured paper, rounded scissors (used with an adult), glue.

practice.prompt: Put the moves in order for one strip.
Which object is woven?
practice.explanation: Mats are woven with raffia or palm leaves.

practice.prompt: Draw your mat with its colours.
practice.answer: A drawing of a woven mat.
practice.explanation: Show the over and under pattern.

lessons.title: Simple dance steps
lessons.objective: Identify and practise simple dance steps and dance gracefully with others.
lessons.course:
Dancing is moving to music. Simple steps: step to the right, step to the left, clap; turn around; bend and stand up.
We dance in a circle or in pairs, and we follow the rhythm.
lessons.model: The adult shows: right, together; left, together; clap, clap; turn around.
lessons.guided: Learn the steps one by one, then dance them to a song in a circle.
lessons.exercise: Say the steps of the dance in order.
lessons.answer: Step right, step left, clap, turn around.
lessons.remediation: Practise only right and left steps with clapping.
lessons.transfer: Teach your dance to a friend.
lessons.materials: Music (a song or a drum), an open space.

practice.prompt: Put the dance steps in order.
practice.answer: right, left, clap twice, turn around.
practice.explanation: Follow the order of the dance.

practice.prompt: How do we dance gracefully?
How many claps in “Clap twice”?

lessons.title: Hopscotch
lessons.objective: Play hopscotch: hop on one foot and land on two feet, following the rules.
lessons.course: Hopscotch is drawn on the ground with numbered squares. We throw a stone into a square, then hop on one foot in the single squares and land on two feet in the double squares, without stepping on the lines or in the square with the stone.
lessons.model: Bih throws her stone into square 3. She hops: 1, 2, jumps over 3, lands on 4 and 5 with two feet.
lessons.guided: Draw a hopscotch with numbers 1 to 8. Take turns to play.
lessons.exercise: Can we step on the lines in hopscotch?
lessons.remediation: Hop on two feet in all squares first.
lessons.transfer: Teach hopscotch to a younger child.
lessons.materials: Chalk, a flat stone, an open space.

practice.prompt: How many squares are in our hopscotch (1 to 8)?
How do we land in a double square?
practice.explanation: Double squares: one foot in each.

practice.prompt: Put the turn in order.
items: Pick up the stone on the way back.
practice.explanation: These are the rules of a turn.

lessons.title: A traditional game of our community
lessons.objective: Describe a traditional game, play it with others and learn from it.
lessons.course:
Children in Cameroon play traditional games: songo (a game with seeds and holes), hiding games, circle games with songs, games with stones.
Games teach us to count, to wait our turn and to play together.
lessons.model: Grandmother teaches Neba a circle game with a song in her language. Everybody holds hands and turns.
lessons.guided: Ask an elder to teach you a traditional game. Play it with the family and say its name in the family language.
lessons.exercise: What does a traditional game teach us?
lessons.answer: To count, to wait our turn and to play together.
accept: To count, to wait our turn and to play together
lessons.remediation: Play a simple circle game first.
lessons.transfer: Teach the game to friends at school.
lessons.materials: Seeds or stones for a game; an open space.

practice.prompt: Which game is played with seeds and holes?
practice.explanation: Songo is played with seeds and holes.

practice.prompt: Say the name of a game in your family language.
practice.answer: The name of a game in the family language.

practice.prompt: Put in order how we play a circle game.
practice.explanation: Circle games begin by holding hands.

lessons.title: The remote control
lessons.objective: Describe the use of a remote control for a radio or a television.
lessons.course:
A remote control lets us use a television or a radio from far. It has buttons: on/off, volume up and down, channel up and down.
We point it at the device and press one button gently. We keep it in its place.
lessons.model: Papa points the remote control at the television, presses on/off, then volume down because the baby is sleeping.
lessons.guided: Look at a remote control with an adult. Find the on/off button and the volume buttons.
lessons.exercise: Which button makes the sound lower?
lessons.transfer: Ask permission before using the remote control at home.
lessons.materials: A remote control (used with an adult) or a drawing.

practice.prompt: Match each button with what it does.
practice.answer: on/off: start/stop; volume up: louder; channel: change programme.

practice.prompt: Where do we point the remote control?
Why do we keep the remote control in its place?
practice.answer: So that we can find it and it does not break.
practice.explanation: Taking care of devices is good.
